title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
claim: Ligand-controlled hydrolysis, using peripheral polydentate ligands to limit lanthanide hydrolysis and stabilize discrete hydroxo species, is the established route to polynuclear lanthanide clusters, but without anion templates it mainly yields low-nuclearity species (typically fewer than 20 metal ions).
explanation: The review traces the approach from tetranuclear {Ln4(μ3-OH)4} amino-acid complexes at elevated pH to the now standard ligand-controlled hydrolysis strategy. Carboxylates, amino acids, Schiff bases, diketonates, phosphonates/sulfonates, polyoxometalates and other polydentate ligands are cited as suitable hydrolysis-limiting ligands, yet the authors explicitly state that clusters made this way without anion templates remain low-nuclearity.
scope: Homometallic lanthanide hydroxide clusters assembled under ligand-controlled hydrolysis.
conditions: Outcome depends on metal-ion source, metal/ligand ratio, pH, solvent, temperature and reaction duration; early tetranuclear amino-acid examples were isolated near pH 6–7 rather than the previously used pH 4.
caveats: The <20 nuclearity statement is the authors’ generalization over the ligand families they list, not a strict physical limit.
